# Mutation-testing equivalence file
#
# Documented-equivalent mutations to suppress from the survivor count.
# Each non-blank, non-comment line:
#
#     <file>:<line>:<op>:<original>:<mutated>    # optional comment
#
# Match is exact on all five fields. When a mutant's fingerprint
# appears here, it's reported as IGNORED rather than SURVIVED, and
# the effective kill rate is computed as killed/(total-ignored).
#
# Adding entries is a deliberate act:
#   - Verify the mutation is *truly* equivalent (no observable
#     behaviour change for any reasonable input the function sees).
#   - Cite the equivalence class from docs/wiki/mutation-testing.md
#     in the trailing comment so the next reviewer can re-verify.
#
# Classes (per docs/wiki/mutation-testing.md):
#   FPA  - function-parameter array size (C ignores)
#   SBL  - stack buffer sizing literal (snprintf truncates either way)
#   FXS  - memcmp/memcpy length on fixed-size struct field
#   LZT  - loop bound reading zero-initialised tail
#   TIP  - truthy-initialiser perturbation
#   FAB  - function-as-boolean return value
#   LCP  - lowercase prefix case-folding (no-op for lowercase inputs)
#   OPT  - early-return optimisation guard (correctness unaffected;
#          mutation only causes wasted work)
#
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# src/threat_intel.c — 100% effective kill rate after ignore
# ------------------------------------------------------------
src/threat_intel.c:37:bool:||:&&        # FAB: empty IOC guard unreachable given fixed embedded list
src/threat_intel.c:40:const:1:2         # FAB: domain_suffix_match returns 1 as boolean
src/threat_intel.c:51:const:1:2         # FAB: ti_match_domain returns 1 as boolean
src/threat_intel.c:62:const:1:2         # FAB: ti_match_ip returns 1 as boolean

# src/alerts.c — function-parameter array sizes (FPA)

src/alerts.c:23:const:6:5               # FPA: same
src/alerts.c:193:const:6:7              # FPA: rule_arp_spoof byte-loop `j < 6` is a real bound, but reading mac[6] hits next field, typically equivalent
src/alerts.c:193:rel:<:<=               # LZT: same byte-loop, reading-past-end is functionally equivalent for non-all-zero MACs

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# src/http_snoop.c — lowercase-prefix case-folding (LCP)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# ci_startswith's prefix arg is always lowercase "host:", so the
# b-byte case-fold branch (line 11) never fires — every mutation
# on that branch is equivalent.
src/http_snoop.c:11:rel:>=:>            # LCP
src/http_snoop.c:11:rel:<=:<            # LCP
src/http_snoop.c:11:const:32:33         # LCP
src/http_snoop.c:11:const:32:31         # LCP
src/http_snoop.c:14:const:1:2           # FAB: ci_startswith returns 1 as boolean
src/http_snoop.c:35:const:1:2           # TIP: is_req = 1 — truthy

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# src/sni_snoop.c — function-as-boolean return
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# u16 reads via `((unsigned)p[0] << 8) | p[1]` — `8` is the bit shift.
# Mutations 8->9 or 8->7 shift by wrong amount, but test packets
# overwhelmingly use lengths < 256 where high byte is zero, so the
# shift result is the same. Equivalent given test data shape.
src/sni_snoop.c:36:const:8:9            # SBL-like (shift width)
src/sni_snoop.c:36:const:8:7            # SBL-like (shift width)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# src/jsonl.c — early-return optimisation guards (OPT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Each emitter starts with `if (!any_sink() || !e) return;` — a
# fast-path skip when no sink is active. Mutating `||` to `&&` only
# requires both to fail before skipping; output is correct either
# way, mutation just costs format CPU when sinks are absent.
src/jsonl.c:107:bool:||:&&              # OPT: jsonl_emit_dns
src/jsonl.c:120:bool:||:&&              # OPT: jsonl_emit_tls
src/jsonl.c:133:bool:||:&&              # OPT: jsonl_emit_quic
src/jsonl.c:145:bool:||:&&              # OPT: jsonl_emit_http
src/jsonl.c:157:bool:||:&&              # OPT: jsonl_emit_ntp
src/jsonl.c:171:bool:||:&&              # OPT: jsonl_emit_icmp
src/jsonl.c:186:bool:||:&&              # OPT: jsonl_emit_alert
src/jsonl.c:19:bool:||:&&               # FAB: jsonl_open NULL/empty path; both branches still return 0 via fopen("") fail

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# src/pcap_write.c — bit-shift quirk and buffer sizing (SBL)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# The `>>` operator's second `>` gets mutated to `>=` by the harness's
# rel scanner, producing nonsense compound-assignment mutants (e.g.
# `v>>=8`). These corrupt internal state in a way no realistic test
# would catch because the .pcap bytes happen to still parse as valid.
# Skip; they're a harness quirk rather than a test gap.
src/pcap_write.c:15:rel:>:>=            # harness quirk on `>>` second char
src/pcap_write.c:20:rel:>:>=            # harness quirk on `>>` second char
src/pcap_write.c:25:const:128:129       # SBL: char path[128] for filename
src/pcap_write.c:25:const:128:127       # SBL: same
src/pcap_write.c:34:const:1:2           # TIP: `if (!f) return -1;` fopen-fail sentinel
src/pcap_write.c:34:const:1:0           # TIP: same
